newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank union prepares nationwide protest day.
newsitem.headline: German bank union prepares nationwide protest day.

text.p: German white-collar workers union DAG, Deutsche Angestellten- Gewerkschaft, said on Monday it was planning a nationwide day of protest later this week against cuts to worker sick pay entitlements by top banks.

DAG, who gave no further details of the industrial action except that it was planned for the second half of the week, said it was also polling bank employees on their willingness to strike on the issue.

Germany's top three banks, Deutsche Bank, Dresdner Bank and Commerzbank have all said they are implementing a controversial new law cutting sick pay from the current 100 percent of salary to 80 percent.

Unlike workers in the metal and engineering sectors, where huge protests against the cuts have taken place, bank employees acknowledge that their contracts do not specifically exclude a cut in sick payments.

DAG earlier this month also urged worker councils at banks to instruct bank employees not to work the overtime it thinks will be necessary to prepare Deutsche Telekom's bourse listing due on November 18.
